    StartersSlaughtered Lamb pork cracklingDry-brined pork rind roasted until blistered and crisp, with flaky saltHow to make it600g pork rind2 tbsp sea salt flakesScore the rind and rub with flaky salt.Dry uncovered in the fridge overnight.Roast at 240°C until blistered and crisp all over.Cool, then break into pieces. Stay on the road.Slaughtered Lamb Scotch eggsSoft boiled eggs wrapped in sausage, crumbed and fried, with English mustardHow to make it5 eggs400g pork sausage mince1/2 cup plain flour100g panko breadcrumbs2 tbsp English mustard1 L vegetable oilBoil four eggs, cool and peel.Wrap each in seasoned sausage mince.Roll in flour, the beaten egg and panko.Deep fry in the vegetable oil at 170°C until deep golden.Halve and serve with English mustard.Wolf enclosure rosemary chilli nutsDavid wakes up naked in the wolf enclosure at the zooHow to make itAs written, serves 4Almonds, cashews and peanuts roasted in egg white, brown sugar, rosemary and cayenne until crunchy, with a scatter of flaky salt.Whisk 1 egg white until frothy.Toss with 150g almonds, 150g cashews and 150g peanuts.Mix 60g brown sugar, 1 tbsp chopped rosemary, half a tsp cayenne and 1 tsp salt and toss through.Spread on a lined tray and roast at 150°C for 30 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes.Cool completely so they crisp, then sprinkle with flaky salt.Pickled eggs from the bar jarKeep off the moors, and beware the moon.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.MainsEast Proctor beer-battered haddockHaddock in crisp ale batter with thick-cut chips, minty mushy peas and malt vinegarHow to make it4 skinless haddock or flathead fillets200g self-raising flour300ml cold pale ale1kg floury potatoes1.5 L vegetable oil, for frying500g frozen peas30g butter1 bunch mint1 lemonmalt vinegarCut the potatoes into thick chips, simmer 5 minutes, drain and dry well.Fry the chips at 160°C for 6 minutes, lift out and rest.Whisk the flour with the cold ale and a pinch of salt into a thick batter.Dust the fish in a little extra flour, dip in the batter and fry at 180°C for 5 to 6 minutes until golden. Keep warm.Fry the chips again at 190°C until crisp.Simmer the peas 5 minutes, drain and crush with the butter, chopped mint and salt. Serve with lemon and malt vinegar.Moors shepherd's pieLamb mince in tomato and Worcestershire gravy under baked mashed potatoHow to make it750g lamb mince1 brown onion, diced2 carrots, diced2 tbsp tomato paste2 tbsp Worcestershire sauce250ml beef stock1kg potatoes60g butterBrown the lamb.Add the onion, carrots, tomato paste, Worcestershire and stock and simmer.Boil the potatoes and mash with butter.Top the lamb with mash and bake at 200°C until golden.SweetsPiccadilly jam roly-polyBaked jam roll pudding served with hot custardHow to make it250g self-raising flour125g cold butter, grated30g caster sugar150ml water200g raspberry jam500ml vanilla custardMix the flour, butter, sugar and water into a dough.Roll to a rectangle and spread with jam.Roll up.Bake at 180°C.Heat the custard and serve alongside.DrinksSlaughtered Lamb mulled aleEnglish ale warmed with spices and orange, with brandy stirred inHow to make it2 L English ale (4 bottles of 500 ml)3 tbsp brown sugar1 cinnamon stick4 cloves2 strips of orange peel1/4 tsp nutmeg, freshly grated80ml brandyPour the ale into a saucepan with the sugar, cinnamon, cloves, orange peel and nutmeg.Heat gently, keeping it well under a simmer so the alcohol stays.Stir in the brandy.Strain into heatproof mugs and serve steaming.Pint of Yorkshire bitterDrink up under the pentagram. Nobody will explain it.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.
